title: Request microfolds: priority-translation memo
body:
Purpose:
This working memo translates a noisy set of customer asks into small, testable proposals ("microfolds") that product and eng can triage quickly. Goal: surface cheap fixes and clear acceptance checks we can ship in 1-4 sprints, plus a small list of higher-effort bets.

Context / input sources summarized:
- 23 support threads (enterprise & startup), recent NPS follow-ups, and 5 voice calls over May–Jun 2026.
- Common channels: customer portal tickets (sample ids in linked_artifacts), field notes from SEs (Rosa), and a short UX test run (10 sessions) run by Jordan.

Top emergent themes (compressed):
1) Response determinism: customers want predictable output for reranks and cached prompts (avoid surprising hallucinations on retries).
2) Cost vs quality controls: easy knobs to trade compute for token quality at route level.
3) Observability gaps: token-level cost breakdowns are useful but hard to map to routes and tooling.
4) Private deployment friction: network egress, KMS enrollment, and install scripts are fragile for air-gapped installs.
5) Retry/fallback semantics: unclear behavior when Dedicated capacity is constrained — customers want explicit SLA fallback policies.

Microfolds (unit proposals) with priority translation:
A. Deterministic-prefix toggle (Priority: High, Effort: S)
- What: New request flag `deterministic_prefix=true` that pins prefix generation to cached KV and disables stochastic sampling for the first N tokens (configurable).
- Why: Several customers reported that repeated calls to the same prompt sometimes return variations that break downstream deduping. Cheap win that uses existing KV-cache + sampling override.
- Acceptance: added flag in API; unit test that same prompt with same KV returns identical first-30-token prefix across 100 runs; doc and example in quickstart.
- Risk: small perf overhead when checking caches; guard by making it opt-in.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Ethan) + product-hosted-api (Jordan).

B. Route-level quality slider (Priority: High, Effort: M)
- What: UI/API field allowing teams to select presets {fast, balanced, high-quality} which map to batching, temperature, and kernel selection profiles.
- Why: Customers asking for a single knob rather than tuning multiple low-level configs.
- Acceptance: presets visible in Console; can be set per-route; telemetry shows expected delta in latency and cost for each preset (compare baseline).
- Owner: product-hosted-api + console-and-rollouts.

C. Token attribution trace snippets (Priority: Medium, Effort: M)
- What: Small console view that maps a response to approximate token-cost buckets (model compute, cache hits, streaming overhead) and links to recent calls for that route.
- Why: Customers cannot quickly understand cost spikes. This is lighter than full token-level trace but actionable.
- Acceptance: prototype view with synthetic data + one pilot customer (acct: AcmeOps).
- Owner: observability + product-console.

D. Private deploy installer checklist and retry script (Priority: Medium, Effort: S)
- What: A hardened shell installer with improved error messages, automated KMS handshake retry, and a post-installation checklist doc.
- Why: Field installs failed on KMS timing and ephemeral DNS; SEs currently do manual steps.
- Acceptance: installer completes full flow in local air-gapped simulation; checklist used by two onboarding customers.
- Owner: private-deployments + solutions-engineering.

E. Explicit fallback policy UI (Priority: Medium, Effort: M)
- What: UI to configure per-tenant fallback sequences (e.g., model->model-quantized->regional-fallback->error-code). Option to auto-promote compatible variants.
- Why: Customers want graceful degradation without custom proxy logic.
- Acceptance: route shows fallback behavior in Console and logs show triggered fallbacks; one staged rollout to an internal test org.
- Owner: console-and-rollouts + serving-runtime.

Sample customer quotes (redacted):
- "We often re-run the same prompt for dedupe and get different IDs — makes our DB messy." (mid-market search infra)
- "We need a single setting to trade quality vs cost per endpoint — our product folks are not ML ops." (SaaS product)
- "Installer failed halfway; KMS key not enrolled and there was no clear retry path." (regulated finance pilot)

Quick fixes (ship in <2 sprints):
- Add `deterministic_prefix` flag and docs (A).
- Add two Console presets `fast` and `balanced` with default mappings; hide advanced toggles behind an \"expert\" section (part of B but can ship fast).
- Build a private-deploy post-install checklist doc and share with SEs for immediate use (D).

Medium-term experiments (2–6 sprints):
- Implement complete route-level quality slider with telemetry hooks (B).
- Prototype token attribution snippets with synthetic run and one customer pilot (C).
- Implement fallback sequence UI with a rule engine for promoting compatible variants (E).

Metrics to track (proposed):
- Rate of repeat-variation incidents per 1k identical prompts (pre/post A).
- Average latency and token cost per preset (for B).
- Number of private-install failures per 100 installs (post D).
- Fallback activations per route and time-to-recover (post E).

Acceptance criteria — explicit tests we can run:
- Deterministic-prefix: 100 identical runs -> identical prefix in 99/100 baseline but 100/100 with flag on.
- Presets: median latency for `fast` is >= 20% lower than `balanced` on typical workloads.
- Installer: zero manual KMS retries required in automated sim.

Unknowns / open questions for triage:
- How does deterministic-prefix interact with existing cache eviction heuristics? (SRE input needed)
- Do customers prefer toggle-per-request or config-per-route for the quality slider? (UX research)
- Privacy/legal implications of token attribution traces in regulated environments? (security/compliance check)

Proposed next steps / short roadmap:
1) This week: Share memo with eng leads + SEs; pick owners for A/B/C/D/E.
2) Sprint 1 (2 weeks): Implement A + quick Console presets; publish docs and internal KB.
3) Sprint 2–3: Build medium-fidelity prototype of C + start B core mapping.
4) Sprint 4–6: Pilot E with two customers and iterate.

Owners & suggested leads:
- A: Ethan Moore (eng-serving-runtime)
- B: Jordan Patel (product-hosted-api) + Console PM (TBD)
- C: Observability eng lead (Rosa to coordinate)
- D: Private deployments (Maya + Solutions Eng)
- E: Console + Serving Runtime (cross-team)

Estimated effort shorthand: S=~3-10 dev days, M=~3-6 dev-weeks, L=>6 weeks.

Draft notes to field:
- SEs: try `deterministic_prefix` with two pilot customers who reported dedupe issues; report back logs.
- Customer success: ask pilot customers if they prefer per-request toggle or route-level default for quality slider.

Appendix: sample API usage (draft)
POST /v1/generate
headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>
body: {
  "model": "rwd-3b",
  "prompt": "<text>",
  "deterministic_prefix": true,
  "route_preset": "balanced"
}

Notes (meta):
- This doc intentionally compresses many customer quotes into omnibus themes to avoid signal fragmentation.
- Plan to convert to a short one-pager for exec review if owners agree on priorities.

Last updated: 2026-06-26 (minor clarifications after SE sync).
